title: Forearm_Hypertrophy_Program_v2
author: P Gree
desc: Unleash your grip strength and sculpt impressive forearms with the Forearm Hypertrophy Program v2. Over the course of one week, you'll engage in five targeted workouts designed to maximize muscle growth and enhance your overall lifting performance. This program combines a variety of exercises focusing on both flexors and extensors, ensuring balanced development. Follow the outlined exercises without changing times or weight for 4 weeks and then increase volume.

ex.note: Heaviest gripper you can close for the full rep range. Rotate hands, rest 45 s between sets.
Palms up, forearms on thighs or bench, full ROM. Fight the handle's urge to roll out — that anti-rotation demand is the upgrade over a fixed handle.
Active grip — squeeze the bar hard. Don't just hang limp. Add a plate via dip belt once 45 s is comfortable.
Light enough to complete both directions without dropping. Each up + down cycle = 1 set.
Load the back of the hand, not the grip. Full ROM with a deep stretch at the bottom. Actually push to extensor failure here — that's the point of the tool.
After your 4 working sets: lighter load, 4–5 sec lowering only (no concentric). Run this immediately after the 4th set.
Grip near end of handle. Lift via wrist only in a 'thumbs-up' arc — isolates extensor carpi radialis which the Finisher doesn't hit as directly. · Weights: 4 lb
Place fingertips inside an open CoC gripper and spread/press against its light tension. Keeps extensors balanced with flexors.
Two plates smooth-side-out, or single plate if that's your limit. Reset grip fully between sets.
Neutral grip, row handle to torso. Rotating handles demand sustained crush and wrist stability through the full pull — brachioradialis activates heavily via the neutral grip.
Shift bodyweight to one arm at a time on the bar — builds asymmetric support grip and forearm stabilisers.
Close a gripper ONE level above your current max (assisted if needed), then fight the opening for 4–5 sec. Eccentric overload drives tendon adaptation.
Grip near end of handle. Wrist moves ONLY side-to-side — forearm stays still. One set = 10 radial + 10 ulnar each arm. · Weights: 4 lb
Elbow pinned to your side. Rotate hammer head like turning a key — full pronation to full supination. Slow and controlled. · Weights: 4 lb
Single rotating handle. Resist it spinning open or closed — trains the 'cup' position used in armwrestling and general rotational wrist control.
Reverses the emphasis from Day 1 — prioritises eccentric loading of the flexors and concentric of the extensors.

ex.n: ★ DRRH Wrist Curl ↔ Forearm Finisher Extension — Superset
ex.note: No rest between the two exercises. 45 s rest between rounds. Flexors then extensors back-to-back — best pump of the week.
Trainer → #0.5 → #1 → up to your current max-closeable level. No rest between rungs. Stop at the first gripper you can't close cleanly.
Add a light plate via dip belt if bodyweight is comfortable for 45 s. Build time before load.
One full up-and-down cycle = 1 set. Match whichever direction feels weakest with slightly slower tempo.
